newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong, Shanghai ties seen unique, competitive.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong, Shanghai ties seen unique, competitive.

text.p: The return of Hong Kong to China this year will put the cities of Hong Kong and Shanghai at the centre of a unique and competitive relationship, experts said on Thursday.

Hong Kong will continue to dominate as a free port and developed financial market, but Shanghai's broader industrial base will ensure its dominance in many areas, speakers at a session of the International Chamber of Commerce said.

"China is growing fast enough to have two major cities," said Philip Bowring, a columnist for the International Herald Tribune. "But Shanghai wishes to establish itself as the premier of the two cities."
"Shanghai is playing catch-up, and to the extent that it is clearly running very hard, the gap between the two cities will narrow quite quickly," he said.
Kenneth S. Courtis, first vice president of Deutsche Bank Capital Markets (Asia), said Hong Kong's financial markets would remain unrivalled by China for a number of years.
The territory, which reverts to China on July 1, would be able to focus on offshore banking, fund management and other financial services, Bowring said.
China's central government had chosen Shanghai as the country's financial capital and had introduced a number of reforms, but it still lagged behind Hong Kong, he said.
Zhao Qizheng, first vice mayor of Shanghai, said the relationship between the two cities would be "unique" and that there was room for more than one financial centre in China.
"Shanghai and Hong Kong will join hands like brothers to move forward and make new contributions to the economic development of Asia," he said.
